entries.title: II Corinthians 10:1
segments: Now, I, Paul, make a personal appeal to you by the meekness and gentleness of the Christ--I who, "in your presence, am humble in my bearing towards you, but, when absent, am bold in my language to you"--

entries.title: II Corinthians 10:2
segments: I implore you not to drive me to "show my boldness," when I do come, by the confident tone which I expect to have to adopt towards some of you, who are expecting to find us influenced in our conduct by earthly motives.

entries.title: II Corinthians 10:3
segments: For, though we live an earthly life, we do not wage an earthly war.

entries.title: II Corinthians 10:4
segments: The weapons for our warfare are not earthly, but, under God, are powerful enough to pull down strongholds.

entries.title: II Corinthians 10:5
segments: We are engaged in confuting arguments and pulling down every barrier raised against the knowledge of God. We are taking captive every hostile thought, to bring it into submission to the Christ,

entries.title: II Corinthians 10:6
segments: And are fully prepared to punish every act of rebellion, when once your submission is complete.

entries.title: II Corinthians 10:7
segments: You look at the outward appearance of things! Let any one, who is confident that he belongs to Christ, reflect, for himself, again upon the fact--that we belong to Christ no less than he does.

entries.title: II Corinthians 10:8
segments: Even if I boast extravagantly about our authority--which the Lord gave us for building up your faith and not for overthrowing it--still I have no reason to be ashamed.

entries.title: II Corinthians 10:9
segments: I say this, that it may not seem as if I were trying to overawe you by my letters.

entries.title: II Corinthians 10:10
segments: For people say "His letters are impressive and vigorous, but his personal appearance is insignificant and his speaking contemptible."

entries.title: II Corinthians 10:11
segments: Let such a man be assured of this--that our words in our letters show us to be, when absent, just what our deeds will show us to be, when present.

entries.title: II Corinthians 10:12
segments: We have not indeed the audacity to class or compare ourselves with some of those who indulge in self-commendation! But, when such persons measure themselves by themselves, and compare themselves with themselves, they show a want of wisdom.

entries.title: II Corinthians 10:13
segments: We, however, will not give way to unlimited boasting, but will confine ourselves to the limits of the sphere to which God limited us, when he permitted us to come as far as Corinth.

entries.title: II Corinthians 10:14
segments: For it is not the case, as it would be if we were not in the habit of coming to you, that we are exceeding our bounds! Why, we were the very first to reach you with the Good News of the Christ!

entries.title: II Corinthians 10:15
segments: Our boasting, therefore, is not unlimited, nor does it extend to the labors of others; but our hope is that, as your faith grows, our influence among you may be very greatly increased-- though still confined to our sphere--

entries.title: II Corinthians 10:16
segments: So that we shall be able to tell the Good News in the districts beyond you, without trespassing on the sphere assigned to others, or boasting of what has been already done.

entries.title: II Corinthians 10:17
segments: 'Let him who boasts make his boast of the Lord.'

entries.title: II Corinthians 10:18
segments: For it is not the man who commends himself that stands the test, but the man who is commended by the Lord.
